scope: Public-source historical metadata inventory for the September 11, 2001 attacks, investigations, response, and documentary record.
source_priority: Official U.S. Government and archival sources prioritized; secondary sources are not treated as equivalent to official findings.

major_source_collections.name: 9/11 Commission Records
major_source_collections.note: NARA states that the Commission transferred legal custody of its records to NARA in 2004 and that the collection contains approximately 570 cubic feet of textual records, including classified material.

major_source_collections.name: FAA 9/11 Records
major_source_collections.note: NARA describes 126 cubic feet of FAA records concerning the attacks, Flights 11, 77, 175 and 93, and subsequent government actions; digitized processed records are available through the NARA Catalog/finding aid.

major_source_collections.name: 9/11 Commission Final Report
major_source_collections.organization: National Commission on Terrorist Attacks Upon the United States
major_source_collections.note: The Commission's mandate covered the circumstances surrounding the attacks, preparedness, immediate response, and recommendations to prevent future attacks.

major_source_collections.name: NIST World Trade Center Investigation
major_source_collections.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
major_source_collections.note: NIST investigated construction, materials, technical conditions, evacuation, and emergency response. It reports extensive interviews and analysis of structural, video, photographic, and audio evidence.

causality_rule: Temporal proximity, metadata correlation, or an unusual record does not by itself establish causation. Causal claims require documentary evidence, validated analysis, or an official finding appropriate to the claim.
privacy_security_boundary: no nonpublic intelligence sources or methods
status: Public historical metadata inventory prepared from official archival, investigative, and government sources. It catalogs sources and metadata rather than copying entire underlying records.
